ev.q: In October 2010, ACIP approved the adult immunization schedule for 2011, which includes several changes.

public_health_question.v: Which vaccines are recommended for U.S. adults in 2011, by age group and medical or other indications, and what changed from the previous schedule?

ev.q: Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule — United States, 2011
ACIP reviews the recommended adult immunization schedule to ensure that the schedule reflects current recommendations for the licensed vaccines.
Annual vaccination against influenza is recommended for all persons aged 6 months and older, including all adults.
Tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis (Td/Tdap) vaccination
All adults without evidence of immunity to varicella should receive 2 doses of single-antigen varicella vaccine
HPV vaccination with either quadrivalent (HPV4) vaccine or bivalent vaccine (HPV2) is recommended for females at age 11 or 12 years
A single dose of zoster vaccine is recommended for adults aged 60 years and older
Meningococcal vaccine should be administered to persons with the following indications
any person seeking protection from hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection
any person seeking protection from hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection
Selected conditions for which Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib) vaccine may be used

equity.level_reason: A vaccination schedule with no data; age only defines the adult population and recommendation groups, with no social-position framing.

level_alternative.reason: American Indians/Alaska Natives and MSM are named in recommendation indications, which could be read as descriptors.

ev.q: administration of currently licensed vaccines is commonly indicated for adults ages 19 years and older, as of January 1, 2011.

notes: Guidance statement summarizing ACIP schedule changes; no quantities are reported. The prepass 'prevalence' cue is a travel-indication phrase, not a measure.
view_issues: Figures 1 and 2 (the schedule itself) are present only as brief descriptions.
